content.content:
**Status:** The `check startup` section (under `## check` > `### startup`) is not marked alpha, beta, or experimental. Other sections in this page carry those labels, such as `--assets` ("beta") and `triggers deploy` ("Experimental"), but this one has no label.

**What it does:** The page says it will "Analyze your Worker's startup phase." It reports "bundle size and a summary of local CPU activity" and "saves a detailed CPU profile." The output includes bundle size, gzip size, and a local startup profile with profile window, sampled time, active and idle time, and sample count. A `.cpuprofile` file can be opened in Chrome DevTools or VS Code. Wrangler also generates this profile automatically when a deployment fails with a startup time error.

The page cautions that results are local: "This command measures performance of your Worker locally, on your own machine." It also says not to expect the local duration to match the startup time on Cloudflare.

**Flags:**
- `--args` (optional): Customizes how the Worker is built for analysis. Pass the same arguments you use when deploying, so the analysis matches the deployed build. The page's example is `--args="--no-bundle"`.
- `--worker` (optional): Analyzes a Worker bundle you provide, for Workers not deployed with Wrangler. The value is a file path to a serialized multipart upload.
- `--pages` (optional): Forces Pages treatment for projects without a Wrangler config file that contains `pages_build_output_dir`.

It also accepts the global flags `--help`, `--config`, and `--cwd`.

content.text:
According to Cloudflare's Wrangler docs today, `wrangler check startup` doesn't appear to be alpha anymore. Other items on the same page are labeled beta or experimental, but this command has no label. I didn't run it to check whether the CLI still prints a warning.

The command analyzes your Worker's startup phase. It reports the bundle size and gzipped size, plus a local CPU summary: profile window, sampled time, active and idle time, and sample count. It also saves a `.cpuprofile` file that you can open in Chrome DevTools or VS Code. The measurements come from your own machine, so the docs warn they won't match startup time on Cloudflare.

The optional flags are `--args` (build the Worker the same way you deploy it, e.g. `--args="--no-bundle"`), `--worker` (analyze a bundle you supply) and `--pages`. Wrangler also creates this profile automatically when a deploy fails with a startup-time error.

Sources:
- [Wrangler Workers commands](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/wrangler/commands/workers/)
